title: Whose is this? Kenen …?
summary: Ask whose one thing is using the basic noun and tämä on.
objectives: Ask whose one thing is using the basic noun and tämä on.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Ask about an unspecified owner
paragraphs: Kenen means “whose”, an owner-question form of kuka (“who”). The owner is unspecified, so add no personal possessive suffix.
Use Kenen + basic noun + tämä on?: Kenen pallo tämä on? (“Whose ball is this?”). Kenen tämä pallo on? is also ordinary word order.
Kenen does not establish how many people own the thing or things. Explicit questions about several owners are outside this pattern. Typed and token tasks accept both taught word orders.
keyPoints: no personal suffix on the question noun

steps: Begin with Kenen (“whose”) to ask about an unspecified owner.
Use kirja (“book”) without a personal possessive suffix.
Use tämä on for the one thing being identified.

commonMistakes: Do not add a personal suffix to the question noun.
The number of things does not determine the number of owners.

parts.formation: Kenen is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”). Several things do not by themselves change kenen.
